41534-langford-of-the-three-bars.title: Langford Of The Three Bars
41534-langford-of-the-three-bars.creator: Kate And Virgil D. Boyles
41534-langford-of-the-three-bars.description: A book by Kate And Virgil D. Boyles. ail since sun-up, sitting his saddle with a heavy indifference born of heat and fatigue, began to think it might be that they were describing a circle and the sun was playing them strange tricks.

arxiv-1509-07234.title: Sparsity-based Correction of Exponential Artifacts Thanks: Preprint submitted to Signal Processing (Manuscript) Thanks: Corresponding author: Yin Ding (yd372@nyu.edu)
arxiv-1509-07234.creator: Yin Ding, Ivan W. Selesnick
arxiv-1509-07234.description: A 2015 arXiv research paper by Yin Ding, Ivan W. Selesnick. This paper describes an exponential transient excision algorithm (ETEA). In biomedical time series analysis, e.g., in vivo neural recording and electrocorticography (ECoG), some measurement artifacts take the form of piecewise exponential transients. The proposed method is formulated as an unconstrained convex optimization problem, regularized by smoothed ℓ 1 \ell_{1} -norm penalty function, which can be solved by majorization-minimization (MM) method.

arxiv-2305-08368.title: Invariant curves of quasi-periodic reversible mappings and its application Journal: Journal of Differential Equations
arxiv-2305-08368.creator: Yan Zhuang, Daxiong Piao, Yanmin Niu
arxiv-2305-08368.description: Abstract We consider the existence of invariant curves of real analytic reversible mappings which are quasi-periodic in the angle variables. By the normal form theorem, we prove that under some assumptions, the original mapping is changed into its linear part via an analytic convergent transformation, so that invariants curves are obtained.

arxiv-2308-04398.title: Character-level NMT and language similarity
arxiv-2308-04398.creator: \name Josef Jon \addr jon@ufal.mff.cuni.cz
arxiv-2308-04398.description: A 2023 arXiv research paper by \name Josef Jon \addr jon@ufal.mff.cuni.cz. We explore the effectiveness of character-level neural machine translation using Transformer architecture for various levels of language similarity and size of the training dataset on translation between Czech and Croatian, German, Hungarian, Slovak, and Spanish. We evaluate the models using automatic MT metrics and show that translation between similar languages benefits from character-level input segmentation, while for less related languages, character-level vanilla Transformer-base often lags behind subword-level segmentation.

arxiv-2309-03574.title: Caveat (IoT) Emptor 1 1 footnotemark: 1 : Towards Transparency of IoT Device Presence (Full Version) Conference: Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer and Communications Security; November 26–30, 2023; Copenhagen, Denmark. Proceedings of the 2023 ACM SIGSAC Conference on Computer
arxiv-2309-03574.creator: Sashidhar Jakkamsetti, Youngil Kim, Gene Tsudik
arxiv-2309-03574.description: Abstract . As many types of IoT devices worm their way into numerous settings and many aspects of our daily lives, awareness of their presence and functionality becomes a source of major concern. Hidden IoT devices can snoop (via sensing) on nearby unsuspecting users, and impact the environment where unaware users are present, via actuation.

arxiv-2310-09945.title: SDSS J125417.98+274004.6: An X-ray Detected Minor Merger Dual AGN ⋆ Corresponding author: mmicic@crimson.ua.edu
arxiv-2310-09945.creator: Marko Mićić 1⋆, Brenna N. Wells 1, Olivia J. Holmes 1, Jimmy A. Irwin 1
arxiv-2310-09945.description: Abstract In this paper, we present the discovery of a dual AGN in a ∼ \sim 11:1 minor merger between the galaxy SDSS J125417.98+274004.6 and its unnamed dwarf satellite. We calculated stellar masses of the primary and secondary galaxy to be 2.5 × \times 10 10 M ⊙ and 2.2 × \times 10 9 M ⊙ , respectively.

arxiv-2501-09347.title: UVRM: A Scalable 3D Reconstruction Model from Unposed Videos
arxiv-2501-09347.creator: Shiu-hong Kao, Xiao Li, Jinglu Wang, Yang Li, Chi-Keung Tang, Yu-Wing Tai, Yan Lu
arxiv-2501-09347.description: Abstract Large Reconstruction Models (LRMs) have recently become a popular method for creating 3D foundational models. Training 3D reconstruction models with 2D visual data traditionally requires prior knowledge of camera poses for the training samples, a process that is both time-consuming and prone to errors.

arxiv-2502-12216.title: Tactic: Adaptive Sparse Attention with Clustering and Distribution Fitting for Long-Context LLMs
arxiv-2502-12216.creator: Kan Zhu, Tian Tang, Qinyu Xu, Yile Gu, Zhichen Zeng, Rohan Kadekodi, Liangyu Zhao, Ang Li, Arvind Krishnamurthy, Baris Kasikci
arxiv-2502-12216.description: Abstract Long-context models are essential for many applications but face inefficiencies in loading large KV caches during decoding. Prior methods enforce fixed token budgets for sparse attention, assuming a set number of tokens can approximate full attention. However, these methods overlook variations in the importance of attention across heads, layers, and contexts.

arxiv-2504-04046.title: Obfuscated Consensus
arxiv-2504-04046.creator: James Aspnes, Shlomi Dolev, Amit Hendin
arxiv-2504-04046.description: Abstract The classic Fischer, Lynch, and Paterson impossibility proof FLP (85) ; LAA (87) demonstrates that any deterministic protocol for consensus in either a message-passing or shared-memory system must violate at least one of termination, validity, or agreement in some execution. But it does not provide an efficient procedure to find such a bad execution.

arxiv-2506-00422.title: DYNAC: Dynamic Vocabulary-based Non-Autoregressive Contextualization for Speech Recognition
arxiv-2506-00422.creator: Yui, Yosuke, Muhammad, Yifan, Chyi-Jiunn, Shinji
arxiv-2506-00422.description: Abstract Contextual biasing (CB) improves automatic speech recognition for rare and unseen phrases. Recent studies have introduced dynamic vocabulary, which represents context phrases as expandable tokens in autoregressive (AR) models. This method improves CB accuracy but with slow inference speed.

arxiv-2507-06722.title: On the Effect of Uncertainty on Layer-wise Inference Dynamics
arxiv-2507-06722.creator: Sunwoo Kim, Haneul Yoo, Alice Oh
arxiv-2507-06722.description: Abstract Understanding how large language models (LLMs) internally represent and process their predictions is central to detecting uncertainty and preventing hallucinations. While several studies have shown that models encode uncertainty in their hidden states, it is underexplored how this affects the way they process such hidden states.

arxiv-2512-17160.title: Can Synthetic Images Serve as Effective and Efficient Class Prototypes?
arxiv-2512-17160.creator: Dianxing Shi, Dingjie Fu, Yuqiao Liu, Jun Wang
arxiv-2512-17160.description: Abstract Vision-Language Models (VLMs) have shown strong performance in zero-shot image classification tasks. However, existing methods, including Contrastive Language-Image Pre-training (CLIP), all rely on annotated text-to-image pairs for aligning visual and textual modalities. This dependency introduces substantial cost and accuracy requirement in preparing high-quality datasets.

The genus Cronobacter (formerly called Enterobacter sakazakii ) is composed of five species; C. sakazakii , C. malonaticus , C. turicensis , C. muytjensii , and C. dublinensis . The genus includes opportunistic human pathogens, and the first three species have been associated wit

pmc-11422006.title: A supervised consultation–Liaison psychiatry training model in a general hospital in China
pmc-11422006.creator: Ruixue Sun, Jinya Cao, Yinan Jiang, Yanping Duan, Wenqi Geng, Jing Wei
pmc-11422006.description: Consultation–liaison (CL) psychiatry is becoming a recognized subspecialty in medical settings; it is a branch of psychiatry that addresses the treatment of the medically ill. Training for CL psychiatry is still insufficient in China. We introduce our training model, supervised CL based on the Union Psychosomatic Clinical Approach with Learning Exchange (UPSCALE) model, to improve consultation–liaison skills among psychiatrists.

pmc-11431459.title: An Overview of Interactions between Goat Milk Casein and Other Food Components: Polysaccharides, Polyphenols, and Metal Ions
pmc-11431459.creator: Bohan Ma, Majida Al-Wraikat, Qin Shu, Xi Yang, Yongfeng Liu, Laurent Bazinet
pmc-11431459.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Casein is among the most abundant proteins in milk and has high nutritional value. Casein’s interactions with polysaccharides, polyphenols, and metal ions are important for regulating the functional properties and textural quality of dairy foods. To improve the functional properties of casein-based foods, a deep understanding of the interaction mechanisms and the influencing factors between casein and other food components is required. This review started by elucidating the interaction mechanism of casein with polysaccharides, polyphenols, and metal ions.

pmc-11671264.title: A clinical practical model for preoperative prediction of visual outcome for pituitary adenoma patients in a retrospective and prospective study
pmc-11671264.creator: Zijian Zheng, He Wang, Qianxi Chen, Zhicheng Wang, Jun Fu, Wenjian Fan, Yuanxiang Lin, Dezhi Kang, Changzhen Jiang, Zhangya Lin, Xiaorong Yan
pmc-11671264.description: ObjectivePreoperative prediction of visual recovery after pituitary adenoma resection surgery remains challenging. This study aimed to investigate the value of clinical and radiological features in preoperatively predicting visual outcomes after surgery.MethodsPatients undergoing endoscopic transsphenoidal surgery (ETS) for pituitary adenoma were included in this retrospective and prospective study. Preoperative MRI, visual acuity, visual field, and postoperative visual recovery data were collected.

pmc-11678270.title: The Effects of Antioxidant Cocktail on Ophthalmological Changes Induced by a 60-Day Head-Down Bed Rest in a Randomized Trial
pmc-11678270.creator: Marc Kermorgant, Fanny Varenne, Anne Pavy-Le Traon, Thomas Geeraerts, Lisa Barioulet, Pierre Fournié, Rebecca Billette de Villemeur, Marie-Pierre Bareille, Arnaud Beck, Adrianos Golemis, Inês Antunes, Guillemette Gauquelin-Koch, Vincent Soler, Jean-Claude Quintyn
pmc-11678270.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). Neuro-ophthalmological changes have been reported after prolonged exposure to microgravity; however, the pathophysiology remains unclear. Furthermore, several countermeasures have been suggested to counteract the side effects of microgravity. The objectives of the present study were twofold: (1) to assess the neuro-ophthalmological impact of 60 days of head-down bed rest (HDBR) and (2) to determine the potential effects of an antioxidant cocktail.

pmc-12505049.title: Evaluation of whole-body MRI for cancer early detection in Li-Fraumeni syndrome
pmc-12505049.creator: Peter Sodde, Zerin Hyder, Sarah Pugh, Fiona Lalloo, Richard Martin, Calvin Soh, Jawad Naqvi, Richard Whitehouse, D Gareth Evans, Emma Roisin Woodward
pmc-12505049.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2025). Li-Fraumeni syndrome (LFS) is a high-risk hereditary cancer predisposition syndrome affecting 1 in 5000 individuals. Current standard of care in adults includes annual whole-body MRI (WB-MRI) and MRI brain (MRB) surveillance to enable early cancer detection. We performed a retrospective single-centre study of adults with TP53 pathogenic germline variants or proven somatic mosaicism undergoing annual WB-MRI surveillance between January 2012 and January 2024, and MRB surveillance between August 2017 and January 2024. 325 WB-MRI scans were performed in 75 individuals.

pmc-12645677.title: The association of ZJU index with bowel health in US participants: a cross-sectional study
pmc-12645677.creator: Jie An, Cheng Jiao, Jun Guo, Lipu Zhang, Zhi Li, Guangchao Liu, Yao Zhang, Wei Liu
pmc-12645677.description: BackgroundThis study investigates the association between the Zhejiang University (ZJU) index, a composite metabolic indicator, and bowel health, specifically chronic diarrhea and constipation, using NHANES data (2005–2010).MethodsThis cross-sectional analysis included 11,180 participants. The ZJU index was used as the exposure variable, and bowel conditions were assessed via self-reported symptoms.

pmc-13065063.title: Development of a new sandwich ELISA for the detection of bovine A1 beta-casein
pmc-13065063.creator: Ayumi Watanabe, Tomoe Kobayashi, Anna Okamoto, Daiki Oka, Tomohiro Noguchi, Ren Ozawa, Koumei Shirasuna, Makoto Matsuyama, Takashi Kuramoto
pmc-13065063.description: The bovine genetic variant A2 beta-casein is associated with fewer digestive and absorption issues compared to A1 beta-casein, leading to increased global demand for A2 milk. However, contamination with the A1 variant during collection, transportation, or sterilization of A2 milk poses a risk, necessitating a verification test to ensure A2 milk does not contain A1 beta-casein.

pmc-13242413.title: Patterns, Timing, and Survival of Recurrence After Surgery for Esophageal and Junctional Adenocarcinoma in the European Multicentre ENSURE Study
pmc-13242413.creator: Lucas Goense, Jessie A. Elliott, Sheraz R. Markar, Fredrik Klevebro, Asif Johar, Styliani Mantziari, Pernilla Lagergren, Giovanni Zaninotto, Richard van Hillegersberg, Mark I. van Berge Henegouwen, Magnus Nilsson, George B. Hanna, John V. Reynolds, ENSURE Study Group
pmc-13242413.description: BackgroundFollowing surgery for esophageal cancer, approximately half of patients develop disease recurrence. Analyzing recurrence site, timing, and their impact on postrecurrence survival can guide refinements in postoperative surveillance and therapy. This study aimed to describe the pattern and timing of esophageal cancer recurrence and assess survival patterns by recurrence location.
